source.title: Pruning artificial neural networks: a way to find well-generalizing, high-entropy sharp minima
source.authors: Enzo Tartaglione; Andrea Bragagnolo; Marco Grangetto

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own measurements showing that gradually pruned networks can generalize well at a narrower, sharper minimum, qualifying the claim that sharp minima generalize worse. It also tests related pruning and generalization outcomes.
record.gate_note: Own results include test error under pruning/retraining conditions and training-loss/Hessian comparisons for gradual versus one-shot pruning. PSP measurements are also reported, but are not mapped to a claim version. Statements about cited prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures pruning performance, unscaled Hessian sharpness and PSP entropy. None tests V1–V8. In particular, its narrow-minimum comparison does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or rank training–test generalization gaps. It also does not vary batch size to test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that gradual pruning reaches greater sparsity and accesses well-generalizing narrow minima that the compared one-shot approaches miss. They interpret higher second-order PSP entropy as evidence of more general features and propose potential transfer-learning benefits; transfer performance itself is left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Pruning and retraining comparisons, plus local-minimum and PSP-entropy measurements; not the interventions or measurements specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by dataset and architecture: LeNet-5 on MNIST tolerates much higher pruning than LeNet-5 on Fashion-MNIST, LeNet-300 on MNIST, or ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10. At the highest compression, gradual versus one-shot pruning also differs in minimum width and second-order PSP entropy.

fits_no_version.finding: Retraining recovers performance at moderate sparsity but struggles at high compression; original initialization is only slightly better than fresh random initialization in the reported comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The ability to retrain a pruned architecture depends on compression, architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: At 99.57% pruning, gradually pruned LeNet-5 on MNIST occupies a narrower minimum with lower training loss and slightly better test performance than the selected one-shot solution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian sharpness need not order test performance across gradual and one-shot pruning solutions.

fits_no_version.finding: The selected gradual and one-shot solutions have comparable first-order PSP entropy, while gradual pruning has higher second-order PSP entropy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradual pruning can produce less class-specialized joint activation patterns than one-shot pruning in highly sparse networks.

record.problems: Figures provide most pruning-percentage test-error comparisons without numeric values in the text; method-specific values are not assigned in the supplied flattened figure text. Sharpness comparison is presented for one selected architecture, dataset, and compression level, although authors say the observations apply to other explored cases. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure-only pruning curves are retained as separate condition rows, with unassignable exact values left as figure only.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; pruning is a different intervention.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove those effects.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study challenges a broader claim that narrower minima necessarily generalize worse, not V7's specific correlational claim about magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps. Figure-only values were not reconstructed. The additional PSP-norm result in Figure 3 also fits no supplied version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps. The paper compares sharpness across two pruning solutions, but does not test the version's specified measure.
